subject: general
question: Who is popularly known as the 'Father of Indian Unrest' for his active role in the Indian Independence movement?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bal Gangadhar Tilak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak, a prominent leader of the Indian Independence Movement, was given the title "Father of Indian Unrest" by British colonial authorities.
 
• He was one of the first leaders to advocate for "Swarajya" (self-rule), making it a mass movement among Indians.
 
• Tilak was a founding member of the Indian National Congress (INC) and played a key role in the rise of the Extremist faction within the party.
 
• Through his newspapers like **"Kesari"** (in Marathi) and **"The Mahratta"** (in English), Tilak inspired Indians to resist British rule.
 
• He was associated with the famous slogan, "**Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it**," which became a rallying cry for the independence movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Extremist vs. Moderate Factions in INC:**

 
 
• Moderates believed in petitions, prayers, and peaceful negotiations with the British government.
 
• Extremists, led by Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai (Lal-Bal-Pal), advocated for direct action and mass mobilization to achieve Swaraj.
 
 
 
• **Home Rule Movement (1916):**
 
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant launched the movement to demand self-governance within the British Empire.
 
• The movement strengthened the demand for Swaraj and laid the groundwork for future independence struggles.
 
 
 
• **Ganesh Chaturthi and Shivaji Festivals:**
 
 
• Tilak popularized these festivals to unite Indians and instill a sense of pride in their culture and history.
 
• These public celebrations became platforms for anti-colonial propaganda.
 
 
 
• **Imprisonment and Writings:**
 
 
• Tilak was imprisoned multiple times for his revolutionary writings and speeches.
 
• While in Mandalay Jail (Burma), he wrote the famous book **"Gita Rahasya,"** interpreting the Bhagavad Gita as a call to action.
